title: SamT; a novel peptide modulator of a two-component system revealed by the specific activation of a small RNA in Enterobacteriaceae.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the full open-access text and the data availability statement; listed every supplementary item in the Europe PMC full-text XML (one single file: gkag727_supplemental_file.pdf, 4,695,985 bytes); searched the text and Europe PMC text-mining for any repository accession (GEO, SRA, BioProject, Zenodo, Dryad) and found none, only cited DOIs; tried three download routes for the supplement (Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint, Europe PMC /bin/ path, PMC /bin/ path) and all failed.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about what the supplement contains: Supplementary Tables S1-S3 are strain, plasmid and oligonucleotide lists, S4 is the genome list for a 16S rRNA tree, S5 is the genome list used for Asr/SamT homolog detection, S6 annotates genes on the screen plasmids. Also from the text only: the genetic screen size (~7,500 colonies, 48 bluer, 14 plasmids sequenced) and that all quantitative data are reporter-assay, western-blot and two-hybrid measurements shown in figures.

a1_downloadable.note: No machine-readable dataset exists anywhere: data availability says 'in the article and its online Supplementary material', and the supplement is a single 4.7 MB PDF (name and byte size read from the full-text XML). No GEO, SRA, BioProject, Zenodo or Dryad deposit. Three download routes for that PDF all failed, so even the PDF tables were not retrievable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no label column anywhere. Any target (reporter activity, homolog presence per genome) would have to be built by digitising bar charts from figures or tables embedded in a PDF.

a3_inputs_present.note: No sequence or feature table is provided; the genome lists are names/assembly identifiers in a PDF table, so inputs would need thousands of lookups plus PDF text extraction.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in the paper's figure axes and methods (beta-galactosidase Miller-type units, relative fluorescence), but only in figures, not in any data table I could open.

a5_enough_rows.note: Quantitative measurements are tens of reporter-assay data points across a few dozen strains; the genetic screen produced 14 sequenced plasmids. Far under the ~400-1,500 row floor. Exact genome count for the conservation analysis is in the unretrievable PDF, so null.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; size is not the problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: there is no download whose counts could be compared with the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only semi-large-scale label in the paper (does a genome carry an asr or samT homolog) is the output of BLASTP plus HMMER profile searches run on the genome sequence itself, i.e. computed from the features by another tool, not a measurement.

existing_models.name: MetaPred2CS (support-vector-machine meta-predictor for pairing bacterial two-component system partners, BMC Bioinformatics 2015)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not read; the search result describes it as combining six sequence-based signals (in-silico two-hybrid, mirror-tree, phylogenetic profiling, gene neighbourhood, operon, gene fusion). I did not retrieve its reported numbers.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Search snippet states that two-component partner pairing is highly specific and still needs costly experimental characterisation.

existing_models.name: ORAKLE (deep recurrent neural network for bacterial two-component signalling pairing, bioRxiv 2019)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not read beyond the title/abstract listing; no number retrieved.

existing_models.name: SmORFinder (profile hidden Markov models plus deep learning for small open reading frames in microbial genomes, Cell Host & Microbe 2020)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet: deep models outperform profile HMMs (F1) on small-ORF families absent from training; predictions enriched for ribosome-profiling translation signal. No single number retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Snippet notes small ORFs remain poorly annotated and hidden among random ORFs.

existing_models.name: SProtFP (machine-learning functional classification of prokaryotic small proteins, NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet reports average 10-fold cross-validation ROC-AUC 0.92 (random cross-validation, not a homology-aware split).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Snippet: assigning function to small proteins when sequence homology is low.

existing_models.name: TargetRNA3 (machine learning for prokaryotic small-RNA target prediction, Genome Biology 2023) and sRNARFTarget
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; a 2025 NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics paper reports sensitivity improving from 39% to 48% on high-quality E. coli data when expression compendia are added.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Small-RNA target prediction sensitivity remains low (under ~50%).

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) would be the natural backbone for small-protein sequences
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for 27-amino-acid peptides, but there is no labelled table to fit a head on
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; the paper's supplement is CC BY-NC 4.0

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. In principle UniProt/RefSeq plus the small-protein catalogues (SmORFinder output, SProtFP) could be joined to SamT/Asr homologs, but this paper supplies no identifier table to join on.
integration.join_key: none present in machine-readable form (genome names and assembly identifiers sit inside a PDF table)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written from this paper's data: there is no table of items with a measured outcome to join to anything.

controls.positive_control: None available, because there is no dataset to run a control on. The paper's own internal control is the known MgrB-PhoQ feedback analogy, which is literature, not data.
controls.negative_control: Not applicable without a feature/label table.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible from this paper's data: the quantitative results are tens of reporter-gene measurements shown only as figures, and the only genome-scale annotation is BLASTP/HMMER output rather than a measurement.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a small protein's amino-acid sequence to predict whether it dampens a bacterial sensor kinase's signalling.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on short bacterial protein sequences (tens of amino acids) paired with a measured effect on a sensor-kinase reporter. This paper supplies that for essentially one protein (27-amino-acid SamT) plus a handful of mutants, so the usable example count is tens, not thousands.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be the change in signalling output of the RstB-RstA two-component system (a bacterial sensor kinase plus its partner transcription factor). The ground truth here is beta-galactosidase reporter activity and fluorescent-reporter activity measured in E. coli cultures, reported only inside figure panels.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Microbiologists studying small proteins as regulators of sensor kinases would want a sequence-based predictor, because finding each modulator currently takes a genetic screen. But that predictor needs a many-protein assay dataset, which this paper does not provide.

ml_idea: The only idea the data could support is sequence-to-effect prediction for small bacterial proteins that modulate sensor kinases (SamT/YdgU-like peptides versus RstB), or presence/absence prediction of asr/samT across gamma-proteobacterial genomes. The first has roughly tens of measured examples from this paper; the second has labels that are themselves BLASTP/HMMER calls computed from the same genome sequences that would be the features, so it is leakage by construction. Neither is viable here.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, nothing timed: the entire supplement is one 4.7 MB PDF, so compute is irrelevant; the blocker is that no feature/label table exists at any size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the supplementary files and look for a csv/tsv/xlsx with one row per measured item. Done: there is exactly one file, a PDF, and no repository accession anywhere in the paper. That killed it in one step.

verdict_reason: Classic bench-genetics paper with no deposited machine-readable data: the whole supplement is a single 4.7 MB PDF of figures plus strain/plasmid/oligonucleotide/genome lists, and the quantitative results are tens of reporter-assay points inside figure panels. Fails A1 (nothing downloadable as data), A2 and A3 (no label or feature column; everything would have to be digitised or reconstructed), A5 (tens of measurements, not hundreds), and A8 for the one genome-scale annotation, whose 'label' is BLASTP/HMMER output computed from the same sequences that would be the inputs.
